note: Deterministic a11y rules (labels, heading order, contrast, roles) are handled by axe-core, not by Jev. Only add questions here that a linter genuinely cannot answer.

questions.question: How obvious is the single primary action a first-time user should take in this component?
questions.rationale: A linter can confirm a button exists; it cannot judge whether the user can tell which one matters.

questions.question: Do the error messages in this component tell the user how to fix the problem, rather than only stating that something is wrong?
questions.rationale: Presence of an error message is checkable; whether it is useful is not.

questions.question: If this component shows an empty state, does it offer the user a clear next step rather than being a dead end?
questions.rationale: Dead-end empty states are a common, invisible-to-tooling UX failure.

questions.question: How do the interactive control labels in this component read?
questions.rationale: jsx-a11y can require an accessible name; it cannot tell you the name is meaningless.

questions.question: From the visible text alone, how clearly could a first-time user say what this component is for?
questions.rationale: Comprehension is the whole point of the UI and nothing in CI currently measures it.

questions.question: Are destructive or irreversible actions in this component visually distinguished and guarded by a confirmation step?
questions.rationale: Requires reading intent from copy, which static analysis cannot do.
